# Config reference

Generated by `conductor-docs`. The keys, their types, the rules and the type descriptions are the specification's, [`spec/domains/config.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/spec/domains/config.yaml); each default is what `conductor config show` prints for a file that leaves the key out, read through the same library the binary runs. A key marked required is one whose absence `conductor config validate` refuses. The hand-written [config guide](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/docs/config.md) says which part of conductor reads each key.

> The one file that names conductor's instances, `conductor.config/1`, read from `--config`, else the `conductor-config` setting, else ~/.b10x/conductor/conductor.yaml. An instance is one organization conductor runs: where its repositories come from, where their checkouts are, where conductor keeps its records, state and cache, which harness and model each role runs on, its cadence, thresholds, reports, and who decides each decision class. These types hold the effective config, after defaults; the file may leave out every key of an instance but its name, its sources and its checkouts. No field takes a secret.

## Top level

The file. A key it does not declare is an error, and so is a value that looks like a token. `default` is the instance a command runs when neither `--instance` nor the `conductor-instance` setting names one; it names an instance of the file.

| Key | Type | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | required | `version == "conductor.config/1"` |
| `default` | [InstanceName](#instancename) | none | `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |
| `instances` | list of [Instance](#instance) | required | `instance.name` distinct across `instances`; `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |

## Instance

One instance. A path is written absolute or under `~`, which is the home directory; the effective path is absolute. `operator` is how sessions name the person who decides class O. Absent from the file, `records`, `state` and `cache` are ~/.b10x/conductor/&lt;name>/records, ~/.b10x/conductor/&lt;name>/state and ~/.cache/b10x/conductor/&lt;name>, `repositories` and `reports` are empty, `operator` and `catalog` are absent, and every other absent key is conductor's built-in default.

A key path written `a[].b` is the key `b` of each element of the list `a`. A default that holds `<name>` holds the instance's name.

| Key | Type | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | [InstanceName](#instancename) | required |  |
| `sources` | list of [Source](#source) | required |  |
| `sources[].github` | string | one of `github`, `local`, `gitlab` |  |

| `sources[].gitlab` | string | one of `github`, `local`, `gitlab` |  |

| `roles[].role` | string | required |  |

| `controllers.max_working` | integer | `5` | `max_working >= 1` |
| `controllers.max_subagents` | integer | `4` | `max_subagents >= 1` |
| `repositories` | list of [RepositoryRule](#repositoryrule) | `[]` |  |

## Types

### InstanceName

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.InstanceName`.

### Harness

The file writes a harness in lower case: `claude` or `codex`.

One of `claude` | `codex`. Specified as `conductor.config.Harness`.

### Tokens

A count of tokens. The file writes a whole number, or thousands with `k`: `300k`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Tokens`.

### Gibibytes

A size in GiB (2^30 bytes). The file writes a whole number with `G`: `15G`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Gibibytes`.

### TimeOfDay

A time of day, UTC, `HH:MM`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.TimeOfDay`.

### Source

Where an instance's repositories come from. The file writes `{github: <owner>}`, `{local: <path>}` or `{gitlab: <group or root>}`; a `local` or `gitlab` source may add `exclude: [<path under the root>]`.

A repository is the directory that holds `.git` at depth 1 or 2 under a root (`<root>/<repo>` or `<root>/<group>/<repo>`), named by its path under the root (`<group>/<repo>`); the root is a `local` source's path, and for the checkouts of the other sources `checkouts.root`. A repository whose name is an `exclude` entry, or lies under one, is not listed and not placed. Absent, `exclude` is empty. A `github` source takes no `exclude`: GitHub lists its owner's repositories, and the collectors that read that list do not filter it.

One of the forms the keys table lists. Specified as `conductor.config.Source`.

### GitHubSource

An owner on GitHub, whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `owner`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitHubSource`.

### LocalSource

A directory whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `path`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.LocalSource`.

### GitLabSource

A group (or the root) on a GitLab forge, whose repositories are the instance's. The conductor binary does not read that forge: the collectors record nothing for this source, and conductor reads it through its session's integration and records the rows with the snapshot record commands.

Keys: `group`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitLabSource`.

### Checkouts

The directory holding the instance's checkouts, and the one holding their managed worktrees.

Keys: `root`, `trees`. Specified as `conductor.config.Checkouts`.

### CatalogNames

How a catalog entry's file stem spells a repository's name. The file writes it in lower case: `plain`, the name itself, or `hex`, the lower-case hex of the name's UTF-8 bytes.

One of `plain` | `hex`. Specified as `conductor.config.CatalogNames`.

### Catalog

The instance's catalog: `repository` names a repository whose checkout lies under `checkouts.root`, written as its path under the root; `path` is a directory on that repository's `origin/main`, written relative to its top, whose `.json` files name the cataloged repositories, one file each, the name being the file's stem as `names` spells it. Absent, `names` is `plain`. An instance without a catalog records no catalog membership.

Keys: `repository`, `path`, `names`. Specified as `conductor.config.Catalog`.

### CommandWord

A value a start command passes to the harness as one shell word, unquoted: a role's model, agent or settings file. Letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `:`, `/`, `-` only, so that no shell reads it as more than that word.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.CommandWord`.

### Role

The harness and model one session role runs on, such as `conductor` or `controller`; the harness agent the role starts with, such as `repo-controller`; and the settings file it starts with, written absolute or under `~`. Absent, a role names no agent and no settings file.

Keys: `role`, `harness`, `model`, `agent`, `settings`. Specified as `conductor.config.Role`.

### Controllers

How many controllers of the instance work at once, at most, and how many sub-agents one controller runs at once, at most. Absent, they are 5 and 4.

Keys: `max_working`, `max_subagents`. Specified as `conductor.config.Controllers`.

### RepositoryRule

The activity of the repositories whose name `match` names. The file writes an activity in lower case: `active` or `inactive`.

Keys: `match`, `activity`. Specified as `conductor.config.RepositoryRule`.

### Cadence

How often conductor runs a cycle, when its daily cycle starts, and how often the watch reads the sessions and main's CI. The file writes a duration as a whole number with `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`: `2h`, `180s`.

Keys: `cycle`, `daily`, `watch`, `ci`. Specified as `conductor.config.Cadence`.

### Thresholds

Conductor's context above which it hands over; the filesystem whose free space the disk thresholds read, written absolute or under `~`; free disk under which the watch reports it, from which a further fall is reported again, under which no session starts, and under which a full gate takes a build slot; the size above which a build is expected to write enough to ask for a slot; free disk under which the full-gate watchdog stops the gate's process group and from which it resumes it; and how often the watchdog reads it. Absent, the filesystem is `/`.

Keys: `context_handover`, `disk_path`, `disk_low`, `disk_clear`, `disk_admit`, `build_slot`, `build_size`, `gate_stop`, `gate_resume`, `watchdog_every`. Specified as `conductor.config.Thresholds`.

### Retention

How many snapshots' observations the instance keeps: those of the newest `snapshots` complete ones. Absent, it is 12, a day at the 2-hour cadence.

Keys: `snapshots`. Specified as `conductor.config.Retention`.

### Report

Where a report goes, as whom it is posted, and on which occasions.

Keys: `channel`, `as`, `when`. Specified as `conductor.config.Report`.

### Authority

Who decides a class-C and a class-O decision. The file writes `conductor` or `operator`.

Keys: `class_c`, `class_o`. Specified as `conductor.config.Authority`.

### Activity

One of `active` | `inactive`. Specified as `conductor.direction.Activity`.

### Decider

One of `conductor` | `operator`. Specified as `conductor.decision.Decider`.
